title: Patients Wary of Governments, Companies Pushing AI as a Rural Healthcare Solution
summary: The $50 billion federal Rural Health Transformation Program is set to flood rural America with new AI health tools. That’s despite little evidence on whether health-related AI can improve access to care and patient health in those communities.

title: A Federal Policy Is Complicating How Organizations Battle the Opioid Crisis
summary: Drug test strips are credited with saving lives, but a new policy will limit how funds can be used for them. Advocates of harm reduction strategies who responded to a mass overdose in Baltimore say distributing them will get harder. Federal officials say the strips enable drug use.

title: Same Knee Surgery, Twice the Price: Hospital Monopolies Push Up Healthcare Costs
summary: A federal disclosure rule is offering new insight on the effect of healthcare monopolies on pricing, following a wave of U.S. mergers.

title: Many States Cover Doula Care, but Access to a ‘Birthing Bestie’ Is Often Out of Reach
summary: Virginia Medicaid started covering doula care four years ago. But logistical and administrative challenges leave many expectant parents without the support of a doula.

title: Journalists Cover Cyclospora and Measles Outbreaks, and Changing Health Policies
summary: KFF Health News journalists made the rounds on national and local media recently to discuss topical stories. Here’s a collection of their appearances.

title: Watch: Why Abortions Are on the Rise Since ‘Roe’ Was Overturned
summary: The way people undergo abortions has changed. This video details five things to know.

title: Budget Battle Erupts in Nation’s Capital Over Opioid Settlement Money
summary: Washington, D.C.’s 2027 fiscal-year blueprint reflects a debate playing out around the U.S.: whether opioid settlement money should be used to free up taxpayer dollars by paying for existing responsibilities instead of new programs.

title: Listen to the Latest ‘KFF Health News Minute’
summary: The "KFF Health News Minute" brings original healthcare and health policy reporting from our newsroom to the airwaves each week.

title: Watch: Democratic Senator Proposes a Fix for American Healthcare — Covering All Kids
summary: Sen. Andy Kim of New Jersey wants to offer universal healthcare until age 26. He sat down with KFF Health News’ Julie Rovner to answer the question: “How Would You Fix It?”

title: Medicaid Work Rule Leaves Homeless People in the Cold
summary: Conservatives who have long pushed for Medicaid work requirements often said vulnerable people would get a pass. But the federal government’s list of exemptions left off homeless people.
